newsitem.title: JAPAN: Arrest of Nomura's ex-president 'very grave'--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Arrest of Nomura's ex-president 'very grave'--MOF.

text.p: The arrest of former Nomura Securities Co Ltd president Hideo Sakamaki is very grave and is "beyond words", Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Friday.
"The fact that the head (of Nomura) was suspected and arrested is very grave and is beyond words," Mitsuzuka said.

Mitsuzuka said the ministry will urge the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC), Japan's securities watchdog, to push ahead with its investigation of Nomura, and added that the ministry will take strict measures once the SESC comes out with its recommendations.

Asked whether the ministry was considering new measures to strengthen inspections of financial institutions, Mitsuzuka said the ministry's inspections were being carried out on a regular basis and added that inspections of institutions against which allegations had been made were being carried out based on voluntary reports from those institutions.
"I believe all financial institutions are now carrying out inspections on their own," Mitsuzuka said.

Tokyo prosecutors said earlier on Friday they had arrested Sakamaki on suspicion of conspiring with three Nomura executives to give 38.5 million yen ($331,000) to racketeer Ryuichi Koike in March 1995.
The prosecutors said in a statement that they had arrested Sakamaki on suspicion of violating Japan's securities exchange law and the commercial code.

On the economy, Mitsuzuka was asked about his view following Thursday's release of data showing that industrial output in April fell a preliminary 0.4 percent from the previous month on a seasonally adjusted basis, which was below expectations.
Mitsuzuka said the economy would be affected by a rise in the sales tax that took place in April, but would overcome the effects in the July-September quarter.
"The economy's firmness is growing," he said, adding that not only the Bank of Japan and the government but the markets seemed to share that view.
